data.name: Rabin
data.gender_notes: Rabin is used as a male name in Hindu naming traditions.
data.long_meaning: He who has the feet of a lotus, or one who has the qualities of a lotus. The name Rabin carries the meaning “Lotus-Footed” and is chosen by families in Hindu traditions for the positive qualities it expresses. Linguistically it belongs to the Hindu tradition and is also used in Sanskrit. Parents who choose Rabin usually hope their child will grow to embody lotus-footed and live with faith, good character and purpose.
data.spiritual_meaning: Symbolizes the divine grace of Lord Vishnu and the embodiment of the lotus feet of God.
data.etymology: Rabin belongs to the Hindu linguistic tradition and is used in Hindu naming. Its recorded meaning is “Lotus-Footed.”
data.numerology_meaning: In Pythagorean numerology the letters of Rabin total 8, giving a life-path number of 8. Number 8 is linked with Saturn and with the qualities of ambition, resilience and material success.

historical_references.reference:
Rabin, a king of Magadha, is mentioned in the Buddhist texts as one of the supporters of the Buddha.
Time period: 6th century BCE
Context: Rabin was a patron of the Buddha and is believed to have provided the Buddha with food, shelter, and protection during his travels in Magadha.
